Four Fe – 13Cr – 4Al alloy ingots were made by vacuum induction melting with pure raw materials.
Then the four ingots were homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 3 h and followed by hot-forging into sheets with thickness of ~10 mm.
Then the four ingots were homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 3 h and followed by hot-forging into sheets with thickness of ~10 mm.
The as-forged sheets were hot-rolled at 800 ◦C with a ~70% thickness reduction through 6 passes. The supplementary heating temperature between each pass was 800 ◦C, and the time was 5 min.
After that the hot-rolled plates were cold-rolled with a total ~50% thickness reduction. The final thickness of all the plates is ~1.5 mm.
Then the as-rolled plates were sectioned into small samples by electrical discharge machining (EDM).
These small samples were annealed with different temperatures ranging from 600 ◦C – 1100 ◦C with an interval of 50 ◦C for 30 min followed by air cooling.
